text:
It is truly heartwarming to observe how cinema has so effectively convinced us that the adolescent experience is less about academic pressure and social anxiety, and more about an unprovoked urge to break into synchronized choreography at the drop of a hat. One can only marvel at the efficiency of this narrative device: why bother with the tedious, messy work of actual communication or emotional growth when a well-timed hip-hop routine can resolve a breakup, a bullying incident, or a failing grade? It is a comforting thought that life’s most profound complexities can be distilled into a perfectly lit stage, where the only thing standing between you and resolution is a better beat drop.

But let us turn our gaze from the absurdity of teenage musicals to the equally dramatic, yet far more mundane, reality of the candle. The primary material of a candle is wax. Yes, wax. A simple, solidified fat or oil that stands there, waiting to be melted by the very flame it helps sustain. It is the ultimate symbol of self-sacrifice, or perhaps just poor structural integrity, depending on how long you stare at it before it inevitably collapses into a puddle of its own making.
